findings.description: parseSPAddress() in lib/silent-payments.ts (lines 122-125) uses string-slicing placeholder logic to extract scan and spend pubkeys from a Silent Payment address instead of actual Bech32m decoding. The comment reads: 'For now, derive placeholder keys from the address data.' It takes raw substring characters from the address string (after the sp1q/tsp1q prefix) and pads them to 64 chars with zeros — producing keys that are cryptographically invalid and not derived from the actual address. Any code path using parseSPAddress() (SPScanner, spend-router onchain-sp path) will receive incorrect pubkeys and fail to detect real incoming SP payments even with a running indexer.
findings.recommendation: Replace the placeholder derivation with real Bech32m decoding per BIP-350 + BIP-352. Either add @scure/base (already has Bech32m support) or use the bech32 npm package. Decode the address, split the 66-byte data payload at byte 33 to extract the scan pubkey and spend pubkey. Until real decoding is implemented, throw a NotImplementedError from parseSPAddress() so callers fail loudly rather than silently returning wrong keys.

findings.description: @arxmint/react (packages/react/src/) contains 5 source files — usePayment.ts, QRPayment.tsx, CheckoutForm.tsx, PayButton.tsx, index.ts — with no test directory at all (packages/react/tests/ does not exist). The @arxmint/js package now has tests (fixed this session), but the React package remains untested. usePayment() has stateful payment polling logic with idle/pending/paid/error state transitions that warrant test coverage. This is the integration surface that merchant developers will use to embed checkout flows.
findings.recommendation: Add packages/react/tests/usePayment.test.ts covering: (1) initial state is idle; (2) start() transitions to pending; (3) paid event transitions to paid and calls onSuccess; (4) error transitions to error state with message. Use node:test with a manual mock for ArxMintClient.pollStatus(). QRPayment and CheckoutForm can be snapshot-tested if a lightweight renderer is added.

context.summary: This delta audit found 2 new issues and verified 7 previously-tracked findings as fixed. The merchant deploy wizard is now implemented as a CLI (scripts/merchant-init.sh via arxmint merchant init) with 3-question interactive flow generating docker-compose.merchant.yml — commit ba70053. The @arxmint/js SDK now has tests covering constructor validation, key scoping, and webhook signature round-trips — commit b18499f. One high finding: parseSPAddress() in lib/silent-payments.ts uses string-slicing placeholder logic instead of real Bech32m decoding (explicitly commented as 'For now'), producing cryptographically invalid pubkeys — SP scanning would silently return 0 outputs for all real incoming payments. One low finding: @arxmint/react has no tests while its sibling @arxmint/js now does. Overall feature completeness improved from 77% to 79% — the core payment infrastructure (Cashu, L402, NUT-24, spend router, merchant directory, Nostr auth, wallet vault, LSP, webhooks, managed DNS, LNURL registry) is solid and well-tested. The remaining stub items (Ark, Silent Payments, Fedimint bridge, Phase 3 advanced features) are correctly gated and marked as prototype in the roadmap.
